requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Comments With "$comment"

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Comments With "$comment"

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword
requirements.text: The "$id" Keyword

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword > Identifying the root schema
requirements.text: The root schema of a JSON Schema document SHOULD contain an "$id" keyword with an absolute-URI (containing a scheme, but no fragment).

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword
requirements.text: The absolute-URI form MUST be considered the canonical URI, regardless of the presence or absence of an empty fragment.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword
requirements.text: Therefore, "$id" MUST NOT contain a non-empty fragment, and SHOULD NOT contain an empty fragment.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword
requirements.text: If present, the value for this keyword MUST be a string, and MUST represent a valid URI-reference.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword
requirements.text: This URI-reference SHOULD be normalized, and MUST resolve to an absolute-URI (without a fragment), or to a URI with an empty fragment.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > The "$id" Keyword
requirements.text: The empty fragment form is NOT RECOMMENDED and is retained only for backwards compatibility, and because the application/schema+json media type defines that a URI with an empty fragment identifies the same resource as the same URI with the fragment removed.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$schema" Keyword

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$schema" Keyword

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$schema" Keyword

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$schema" Keyword
requirements.text: If this URI identifies a retrievable resource, that resource SHOULD be of media type "application/schema+json".

requirements.text: The "$vocabulary" Keyword

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword > Default vocabularies
requirements.text: If "$vocabulary" is absent, an implementation MAY determine behavior based on the meta-schema if it is recognized from the URI value of the referring schema's "$schema" keyword.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword > Default vocabularies
requirements.text: If the implementation proceeds with processing the schema, it MUST assume the use of the core vocabulary.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword > Default vocabularies
requirements.text: For example, an implementation that is a validator SHOULD assume the use of all vocabularies in this specification and the companion Validation specification.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword > Default vocabularies
requirements.text: If the implementation is built for a specific purpose, then it SHOULD assume the use of all of the most relevant vocabularies for that purpose.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: The URI MAY be a URL, but the nature of the retrievable resource is currently undefined, and reserved for future use.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: Vocabulary authors MAY use the URL of the vocabulary specification, in a human-readable media type such as text/html or text/plain, as the vocabulary URI.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: Any vocabulary that is understood by the implementation MUST be processed in a manner consistent with the semantic definitions contained within the vocabulary.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: It MUST NOT appear in subschemas.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: The property names in the object MUST be URIs (containing a scheme) and this URI MUST be normalized.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: It is also used to indicate whether each vocabulary is required or optional, in the sense that an implementation MUST understand the required vocabularies in order to successfully process the schema.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: The value of this keyword MUST be an object.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: If the value is true, then implementations that do not recognize the vocabulary MUST refuse to process any schemas that declare this meta-schema with "$schema".

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: The values of the object properties MUST be booleans.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: The "$vocabulary" keyword MUST be ignored in schema documents that are not being processed as a meta-schema.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: Per [extending], unrecognized keywords SHOULD be treated as annotations.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: If the value is false, implementations that do not recognize the vocabulary SHOULD proceed with processing such schemas.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Meta-Schemas and Vocabularies > The "$vocabulary" Keyword
requirements.text: The "$vocabulary" keyword SHOULD be used in the root schema of any schema document intended for use as a meta-schema.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas
requirements.text: This section defines a vocabulary of applicator keywords that are RECOMMENDED for use as the basis of other vocabularies.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas
requirements.text: Meta-schemas that do not use "$vocabulary" SHOULD be considered to require this vocabulary as if its URI were present with a value of true.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Unevaluated Locations
requirements.text: Meta-schemas that do not use "$vocabulary" SHOULD be considered to require this vocabulary as if its URI were present with a value of true.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Objects > additionalProperties
requirements.text: Implementations that do not support annotation collection MUST do so.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Objects > additionalProperties
requirements.text: The value of "additionalProperties" MUST be a valid JSON Schema.

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > Defining location-independent identifiers
requirements.text: If present, the value of this keyword MUST be a string and MUST start with a letter ([A-Za-z]) or underscore ("_"), followed by any number of letters, digits ([0-9]), hyphens ("-"), underscores ("_"), and periods (".").

requirements.section: The JSON Schema Core Vocabulary > Base URI, Anchors, and Dereferencing > Defining location-independent identifiers
requirements.text: Therefore it is RECOMMENDED that "$anchor" be used to create plain name fragments unless there is a clear need for "$dynamicAnchor".

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Annotations > Collecting Annotations > Annotations and Assertions
requirements.text: Schema objects that produce a false assertion result MUST NOT produce any annotation results, whether from their own keywords or from keywords in subschemas.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Annotations > Collecting Annotations
requirements.text: This MAY be omitted if it is the same as the schema location path from above.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Annotations > Collecting Annotations
requirements.text: A collected annotation MUST include the following information:

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Annotations > Collecting Annotations > Distinguishing Among Multiple Values
requirements.text: Applications MAY make decisions on which of multiple annotation values to use based on the schema location that contributed the value.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Annotations
requirements.text: The only exception is that subschemas of a schema object that has failed validation MAY be skipped, as annotations are not retained for failing schemas.

requirements.text: anyOf

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas With Logic > anyOf
requirements.text: This keyword's value MUST be a non-empty array.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas With Logic > anyOf
requirements.text: Note that when annotations are being collected, all subschemas MUST be examined so that annotations are collected from each subschema that validates successfully.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Applicators
requirements.text: Applicators may apply any boolean logic operation to the assertion results of subschemas, but MUST NOT introduce new assertion conditions of their own.

requirements.section: Working with vocabularies > Best practices for vocabulary and meta-schema authors
requirements.text: Such meta-schemas SHOULD not forbid additional keywords, and MUST not forbid any keywords from the Core vocabulary.

requirements.section: Working with vocabularies > Best practices for vocabulary and meta-schema authors
requirements.text: Vocabulary authors SHOULD provide a meta-schema that validates the expected usage of the vocabulary's keywords on their own.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: The key of the "$defs" for the now embedded Schema Resource MAY be the "$id" of the bundled schema or some other form of application defined unique identifer (such as a UUID).

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: A Schema Resource MAY be embedded in a location other than "$defs" where the location is defined as a schema value.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: Each embedded JSON Schema Resource MUST identify itself with a URI using the "$id" keyword, and SHOULD make use of the "$schema" keyword to identify the dialect it is using, in the root of the schema resource.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: A Bundled Schema Resource MUST NOT be bundled by replacing the schema object from which it was referenced, or by wrapping the Schema Resource in other applicator keywords.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: In order to produce identical output, references in the containing schema document to the previously external Schema Resources MUST NOT be changed, and now resolve to a schema using the "$id" of an embedded Schema Resource.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: When the Schema Resource referenced by a by-reference applicator is bundled, it is RECOMMENDED that the Schema Resource be located as a value of a "$defs" object at the containing schema's root.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: It is RECOMMENDED that the URI identifier value of "$id" be an Absolute URI.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Bundling
requirements.text: Bundling SHOULD be done in such a way that all URIs (used for referencing) in the base document and any referenced/embedded documents do not require altering.

requirements.section: ChangeLog
requirements.text: "$schema" MAY change for embedded resources

requirements.section: ChangeLog
requirements.text: "$schema" SHOULD NOT appear in subschemas, although that may change

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents
requirements.text: Each embedded Schema Resource MUST be treated as an individual Schema Resource, following standard schema loading and processing requirements, including determining vocabulary support.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally
requirements.text: "if", "then", and "else" MUST NOT interact with each other across subschema boundaries.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally
requirements.text: In other words, an "if" in one branch of an "allOf" MUST NOT have an impact on a "then" or "else" in another branch.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally
requirements.text: In particular, they MUST NOT be treated as if present with an empty schema, and when "if" is not present, both "then" and "else" MUST be entirely ignored.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: contains

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: This annotation affects the behavior of "unevaluatedItems" in the Unevaluated vocabulary, and MAY also be used to implement the "minContains" and "maxContains" keywords in the Validation vocabulary.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: The value MAY be a boolean "true" if the subschema validates successfully when applied to every index of the instance.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: The annotation MUST be present if the instance array to which this keyword's schema applies is empty.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: An array instance is valid against "contains" if at least one of its elements is valid against the given schema, except when "minContains" is present and has a value of 0, in which case an array instance MUST be considered valid against the "contains" keyword, even if none of its elements is valid against the given schema.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: The subschema MUST be applied to every array element even after the first match has been found, in order to collect annotations for use by other keywords.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Child Instances > Keywords for Applying Subschemas to Arrays > contains
requirements.text: The value of this keyword MUST be a valid JSON Schema.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Default Behaviors
requirements.text: Because annotation collection can add significant cost in terms of both computation and memory, implementations MAY opt out of this feature.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Default Behaviors
requirements.text: However, even if the value which produces the default behavior would produce annotation results if present, the default behavior still MUST NOT result in annotations.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Default Behaviors
requirements.text: A missing keyword MUST NOT produce a false assertion result, MUST NOT produce annotation results, and MUST NOT cause any other schema to be evaluated as part of its own behavioral definition.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Default Behaviors
requirements.text: Keywords that are specified in terms of collected annotations SHOULD describe reasonable alternate approaches when appropriate.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Default Behaviors
requirements.text: In some cases, the missing keyword assertion behavior of a keyword is identical to that produced by a certain value, and keyword definitions SHOULD note such values where known.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > dependentSchemas
requirements.text: dependentSchemas

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > dependentSchemas
requirements.text: Each value in the object MUST be a valid JSON Schema.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > dependentSchemas
requirements.text: This keyword's value MUST be an object.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Dereferencing
requirements.text: If the resulting URI identifies a schema within the current document, or within another schema document that has been made available to the implementation, then that schema SHOULD be used automatically.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Loading a Schema > Detecting a Meta-Schema
requirements.text: Implementations MAY allow a schema to be explicitly passed as a meta-schema, for implementation-specific purposes, such as pre-loading a commonly used meta-schema and checking its vocabulary support requirements up front.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Loading a Schema > Detecting a Meta-Schema
requirements.text: Implementations MUST recognize a schema as a meta-schema if it is being examined because it was identified as such by another schema's "$schema" keyword.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Loading a Schema > Detecting a Meta-Schema
requirements.text: Meta-schema authors MUST NOT expect such features to be interoperable across implementations.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Differing and Default Dialects
requirements.text: Since any schema that can be referenced can also be embedded, embedded schema resources MAY specify different processing dialects using the "$schema" values from their enclosing resource.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Compound Documents > Differing and Default Dialects
requirements.text: When multiple schema resources are present in a single document, schema resources which do not define with which dialect they should be processed MUST be processed with the same dialect as the enclosing resource.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > else
requirements.text: else

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > else
requirements.text: This keyword's value MUST be a valid JSON Schema.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > else
requirements.text: Implementations MUST NOT evaluate the instance against this keyword, for either validation or annotation collection purposes, in such cases.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Dereferencing > JSON Pointer fragments and embedded schema resources
requirements.text: An implementation MAY choose not to support addressing schema resource contents by URIs using a base other than the resource's canonical URI, plus a JSON Pointer fragment relative to that base.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Dereferencing > JSON Pointer fragments and embedded schema resources
requirements.text: Since URIs involving JSON Pointer fragments relative to the parent schema resource's URI cease to be valid when the embedded schema is moved to a separate document and referenced, applications and schemas SHOULD NOT use such URIs to identify embedded schema resources or locations within them.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Dereferencing > JSON Pointer fragments and embedded schema resources
requirements.text: Therefore, schema authors SHOULD NOT rely on such URIs, as using them may reduce interoperability.

requirements.section: General Considerations > Extending JSON Schema
requirements.text: Additional schema keywords and schema vocabularies MAY be defined by any entity.

requirements.section: General Considerations > Extending JSON Schema
requirements.text: Implementations MAY provide the ability to register or load handlers for vocabularies that they do not support directly.

requirements.section: General Considerations > Extending JSON Schema
requirements.text: Save for explicit agreement, schema authors SHALL NOT expect these additional keywords and vocabularies to be supported by implementations that do not explicitly document such support.

requirements.section: General Considerations > Extending JSON Schema
requirements.text: Implementations SHOULD treat keywords they do not support as annotations, where the value of the keyword is the value of the annotation.

requirements.section: Fragment Identifiers
requirements.text: All fragment identifiers that do not match the JSON Pointer syntax MUST be interpreted as plain name fragment identifiers.

requirements.section: Fragment Identifiers
requirements.text: For "application/schema+json", which supports two fragment identifier syntaxes, fragment identifiers matching the JSON Pointer syntax, including the empty string, MUST be interpreted as JSON Pointer fragment identifiers.

requirements.section: Fragment Identifiers
requirements.text: In accordance with section 3.1 of RFC 6839, the syntax and semantics of fragment identifiers specified for any +json media type SHOULD be as specified for "application/json".

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Caveats > Guarding Against Infinite Recursion
requirements.text: A schema MUST NOT be run into an infinite loop against an instance.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Caveats > Guarding Against Infinite Recursion
requirements.text: Schemas SHOULD NOT make use of infinite recursive nesting like this; the behavior is undefined.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Associating Instances and Schemas > Usage for Hypermedia > Linking to a Schema
requirements.text: It is RECOMMENDED that instances described by a schema provide a link to a downloadable JSON Schema using the link relation "describedby", as defined by Linked Data Protocol 1.0, section 8.1.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Associating Instances and Schemas > Usage for Hypermedia > Usage Over HTTP
requirements.text: Clients SHOULD be able to make requests with a "From" header so that server operators can contact the owner of a potentially misbehaving script.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Associating Instances and Schemas > Usage for Hypermedia > Usage Over HTTP
requirements.text: Clients SHOULD set or prepend a User-Agent header specific to the JSON Schema implementation or software product.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Associating Instances and Schemas > Usage for Hypermedia > Usage Over HTTP
requirements.text: Distributed systems SHOULD make use of a shared cache and/or caching proxy.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Associating Instances and Schemas > Usage for Hypermedia > Usage Over HTTP
requirements.text: HTTP clients SHOULD observe caching headers and not re-request documents within their freshness period.

requirements.section: Loading and Processing Schemas > Associating Instances and Schemas > Usage for Hypermedia > Usage Over HTTP
requirements.text: HTTP servers SHOULD set long-lived caching headers on JSON Schemas.

requirements.section: Keyword Behaviors > Identifiers
requirements.text: Canonical schema URIs MUST NOT change while processing an instance, but keywords that affect URI-reference resolution MAY have behavior that is only fully determined at runtime.

requirements.text: if

requirements.text: Instances that fail to validate against this keyword's subschema MUST also be valid against the subschema value of the "else" keyword, if present.

requirements.section: A Vocabulary for Applying Subschemas > Keywords for Applying Subschemas in Place > Keywords for Applying Subschemas Conditionally > if
requirements.text: Instances that successfully validate against this keyword's subschema MUST also be valid against the subschema value of the "then" keyword, if present.

Path templating is allowed. When matching URLs, concrete (non-templated) paths would be matched before their templated counterparts. Templated paths with the same hierarchy but different templated names MUST NOT exist as they are identical. In case of ambiguous matching, it's up to the tooling to decide which one to use.

requirements.section: Appendix D: Serializing Headers and Cookies > Percent-Encoding and Cookies
requirements.text: While percent-encoding seems more common as an escaping mechanism than the base64 encoding (`contentEncoding`: "base64") recommended by [RFC6265], section 5.6 of draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-20, the proposed update to that RFC notes that cookies sent in the `Set-Cookie` response header that appear to be percent-encoded MUST NOT be decoded when stored by the client, which would mean that they are already encoded when retrieved from that storage for use in the `Cookie` request header.

requirements.section: Appendix E: Percent-Encoding and Form Media Types > Percent-Encoding and `form-data`
requirements.text: Users wishing to use percent-encoding in this way MUST provide the data in percent-encoded form, as percent-encoding is not automatically applied for this media type regardless of which Encoding Object fields are used.

requirements.text: For maximum interoperability, it is RECOMMENDED to either define and document an additional escape convention while percent-encoding the delimiters for these styles, or to avoid these styles entirely.

To define a range of response codes, this field MAY contain the uppercase wildcard character `X`. For example, `2XX` represents all response codes between `200` and `299`. Only the following range definitions are allowed: `1XX`, `2XX`, `3XX`, `4XX`, and `5XX`. If a response is defined using an explicit code, the explicit code definition takes precedence over the range definition for that code.

requirements.section: Specification Extensions

requirements.section: Introduction > TLS Version
requirements.text: Implementations MAY also support additional transport-layer security mechanisms that meet their security requirements.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Authentication
requirements.text: The authorization server MAY issue a client password or other credentials for a specific installation of a native application client on a specific device.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Authentication
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST NOT issue client passwords or other client credentials to native application or user-agent-based application clients for the purpose of client authentication.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Authentication
requirements.text: Web application clients MUST ensure confidentiality of client passwords and other client credentials.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Authentication
requirements.text: When client authentication is not possible, the authorization server SHOULD employ other means to validate the client's identity -- for example, by requiring the registration of the client redirection URI or enlisting the resource owner to confirm identity.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Credentials-Guessing Attacks
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST prevent attackers from guessing access tokens, authorization codes, refresh tokens, resource owner passwords, and client credentials.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Credentials-Guessing Attacks
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST utilize other means to protect credentials intended for end-user usage.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Credentials-Guessing Attacks
requirements.text: The probability of an attacker guessing generated tokens (and other credentials not intended for handling by end-users) MUST be less than or equal to 2^(-128) and SHOULD be less than or equal to 2^(-160).

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Phishing Attacks
requirements.text: To reduce the risk of phishing attacks, the authorization servers MUST require the use of TLS on every endpoint used for end-user interaction.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Cross-Site Request Forgery
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST implement CSRF protection for its authorization endpoint and ensure that a malicious client cannot obtain authorization without the awareness and explicit consent of the resource owner.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Cross-Site Request Forgery
requirements.text: The binding value used for CSRF protection MUST contain a non-guessable value (as described in Section 10.10), and the user-agent's authenticated state (e.g., session cookie, HTML5 local storage) MUST be kept in a location accessible only to the client and the user-agent (i.e., protected by same-origin policy).

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Cross-Site Request Forgery
requirements.text: The client MUST implement CSRF protection for its redirection URI.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Cross-Site Request Forgery
requirements.text: The client SHOULD utilize the "state" request parameter to deliver this value to the authorization server when making an authorization request.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Clickjacking
requirements.text: To prevent this form of attack, native applications SHOULD use external browsers instead of embedding browsers within the application when requesting end-user authorization.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Code Injection and Input Validation
requirements.text: The authorization server and client MUST sanitize (and validate when possible) any value received -- in particular, the value of the "state" and "redirect_uri" parameters.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Misuse of Access Token to Impersonate Resource Owner in Implicit
requirements.text: Any specification that uses the authorization process as a form of delegated end-user authentication to the client (e.g., third-party sign-in service) MUST NOT use the implicit flow without additional security mechanisms that would enable the client to determine if the access token was issued for its use (e.g., audience-restricting the access token).

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Impersonation
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST authenticate the client whenever possible.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Impersonation
requirements.text: If the authorization server cannot authenticate the client due to the client's nature, the authorization server MUST require the registration of any redirection URI used for receiving authorization responses and SHOULD utilize other means to protect resource owners from such potentially malicious clients.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Impersonation
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD enforce explicit resource owner authentication and provide the resource owner with information about the client and the requested authorization scope and lifetime.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Client Impersonation
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD NOT process repeated authorization requests automatically (without active resource owner interaction) without authenticating the client or relying on other measures to ensure that the repeated request comes from the original client and not an impersonator.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Access Tokens
requirements.text: Access token credentials MUST only be transmitted using TLS as described in Section 1.6 with server authentication as defined by [RFC2818].

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Access Tokens
requirements.text: Access token credentials (as well as any confidential access token attributes) MUST be kept confidential in transit and storage, and only shared among the authorization server, the resource servers the access token is valid for, and the client to whom the access token is issued.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Access Tokens
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST ensure that access tokens cannot be generated, modified, or guessed to produce valid access tokens by unauthorized parties.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Access Tokens
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD take the client identity into account when choosing how to honor the requested scope and MAY issue an access token with less rights than requested.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Access Tokens
requirements.text: The client SHOULD request access tokens with the minimal scope necessary.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: Authorization servers MAY issue refresh tokens to web application clients and native application clients.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST ensure that refresh tokens cannot be generated, modified, or guessed to produce valid refresh tokens by unauthorized parties.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST maintain the binding between a refresh token and the client to whom it was issued.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST verify the binding between the refresh token and client identity whenever the client identity can be authenticated.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: Refresh tokens MUST be kept confidential in transit and storage, and shared only among the authorization server and the client to whom the refresh tokens were issued.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: Refresh tokens MUST only be transmitted using TLS as described in Section 1.6 with server authentication as defined by [RFC2818].

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Refresh Tokens
requirements.text: When client authentication is not possible, the authorization server SHOULD deploy other means to detect refresh token abuse.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Codes
requirements.text: Authorization codes MUST be short lived and single-use.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Codes
requirements.text: If the client can be authenticated, the authorization servers MUST authenticate the client and ensure that the authorization code was issued to the same client.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Codes
requirements.text: Therefore, if the client relies on the authorization code for its own resource owner authentication, the client redirection endpoint MUST require the use of TLS.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Codes
requirements.text: If the authorization server observes multiple attempts to exchange an authorization code for an access token, the authorization server SHOULD attempt to revoke all access tokens already granted based on the compromised authorization code.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Codes
requirements.text: The transmission of authorization codes SHOULD be made over a secure channel, and the client SHOULD require the use of TLS with its redirection URI if the URI identifies a network resource.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Code Redirection URI Manipulation
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST require public clients and SHOULD require confidential clients to register their redirection URIs.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Code Redirection URI Manipulation
requirements.text: In order to prevent such an attack, the authorization server MUST ensure that the redirection URI used to obtain the authorization code is identical to the redirection URI provided when exchanging the authorization code for an access token.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Authorization Code Redirection URI Manipulation
requirements.text: If a redirection URI is provided in the request, the authorization server MUST validate it against the registered value.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Resource Owner Password Credentials
requirements.text: The authorization server and client SHOULD minimize use of this grant type and utilize other grant types whenever possible.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Request Confidentiality
requirements.text: Access tokens, refresh tokens, resource owner passwords, and client credentials MUST NOT be transmitted in the clear.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Request Confidentiality
requirements.text: Authorization codes SHOULD NOT be transmitted in the clear.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Request Confidentiality
requirements.text: The "state" and "scope" parameters SHOULD NOT include sensitive client or resource owner information in plain text, as they can be transmitted over insecure channels or stored insecurely.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Ensuring Endpoint Authenticity
requirements.text: The client MUST validate the authorization server's TLS certificate as defined by [RFC6125] and in accordance with its requirements for server identity authentication.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Ensuring Endpoint Authenticity
requirements.text: In order to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks, the authorization server MUST require the use of TLS with server authentication as defined by [RFC2818] for any request sent to the authorization and token endpoints.

requirements.section: IANA Considerations > OAuth Access Token Types Registry > Registration Template
requirements.text: New parameters MUST be separately registered in the OAuth Parameters registry as described by Section 11.2.

requirements.section: IANA Considerations > OAuth Extensions Error Registry > Registration Template
requirements.text: Values for the error name MUST NOT include characters outside the set %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Types
requirements.text: If the authorization server does not provide support for such clients or does not provide guidance with regard to their registration, the client SHOULD register each component as a separate client.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Types
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD NOT make assumptions about the client type.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Identifier
requirements.text: The client identifier is not a secret; it is exposed to the resource owner and MUST NOT be used alone for client authentication.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Identifier
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD document the size of any identifier it issues.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: Alternatively, the authorization server MAY support including the client credentials in the request-body using the following parameters:

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: The client MAY omit the parameter if the client secret is an empty string.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: Clients in possession of a client password MAY use the HTTP Basic authentication scheme as defined in [RFC2617] to authenticate with the authorization server.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST require the use of TLS as described in Section 1.6 when sending requests using password authentication.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST support the HTTP Basic authentication scheme for authenticating clients that were issued a client password.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: The parameters can only be transmitted in the request-body and MUST NOT be included in the request URI.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: Since this client authentication method involves a password, the authorization server MUST protect any endpoint utilizing it against brute force attacks.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: Including the client credentials in the request-body using the two parameters is NOT RECOMMENDED and SHOULD be limited to clients unable to directly utilize the HTTP Basic authentication scheme (or other password-based HTTP authentication schemes).

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: client_id REQUIRED.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Client Password
requirements.text: client_secret REQUIRED.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Other Authentication Methods
requirements.text: The authorization server MAY support any suitable HTTP authentication scheme matching its security requirements.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication > Other Authentication Methods
requirements.text: When using other authentication methods, the authorization server MUST define a mapping between the client identifier (registration record) and authentication scheme.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication
requirements.text: The authorization server MAY accept any form of client authentication meeting its security requirements.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication
requirements.text: The authorization server MAY establish a client authentication method with public clients.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication
requirements.text: The client MUST NOT use more than one authentication method in each request.

requirements.section: Client Registration > Client Authentication
requirements.text: However, the authorization server MUST NOT rely on public client authentication for the purpose of identifying the client.

requirements.text: When registering a client, the client developer SHALL:

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Response Type
requirements.text: Extension response types MAY contain a space-delimited (%x20) list of values, where the order of values does not matter (e.g., response type "a b" is the same as "b a").

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Response Type
requirements.text: If an authorization request is missing the "response_type" parameter, or if the response type is not understood, the authorization server MUST return an error response as described in Section 4.1.2.1.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Response Type
requirements.text: The value MUST be one of "code" for requesting an authorization code as described by Section 4.1.1, "token" for requesting an access token (implicit grant) as described by Section 4.2.1, or a registered extension value as described by Section 8.4.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Response Type
requirements.text: response_type REQUIRED.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Endpoint Request Confidentiality
requirements.text: The redirection endpoint SHOULD require the use of TLS as described in Section 1.6 when the requested response type is "code" or "token", or when the redirection request will result in the transmission of sensitive credentials over an open network.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Endpoint Request Confidentiality
requirements.text: If TLS is not available, the authorization server SHOULD warn the resource owner about the insecure endpoint prior to redirection (e.g., display a message during the authorization request).

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Registration Requirements
requirements.text: The authorization server MAY allow the client to register multiple redirection endpoints.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Registration Requirements
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST require the following clients to register their redirection endpoint:

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Registration Requirements
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD require all clients to register their redirection endpoint prior to utilizing the authorization endpoint.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Registration Requirements
requirements.text: The authorization server SHOULD require the client to provide the complete redirection URI (the client MAY use the "state" request parameter to achieve per-request customization).

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Registration Requirements
requirements.text: If requiring the registration of the complete redirection URI is not possible, the authorization server SHOULD require the registration of the URI scheme, authority, and path (allowing the client to dynamically vary only the query component of the redirection URI when requesting authorization).

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Dynamic Configuration
requirements.text: If the client registration included the full redirection URI, the authorization server MUST compare the two URIs using simple string comparison as defined in [RFC3986] Section 6.2.1.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Dynamic Configuration
requirements.text: If multiple redirection URIs have been registered, if only part of the redirection URI has been registered, or if no redirection URI has been registered, the client MUST include a redirection URI with the authorization request using the "redirect_uri" request parameter.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Dynamic Configuration
requirements.text: When a redirection URI is included in an authorization request, the authorization server MUST compare and match the value received against at least one of the registered redirection URIs (or URI components) as defined in [RFC3986] Section 6, if any redirection URIs were registered.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Invalid Endpoint
requirements.text: If an authorization request fails validation due to a missing, invalid, or mismatching redirection URI, the authorization server SHOULD inform the resource owner of the error and MUST NOT automatically redirect the user-agent to the invalid redirection URI.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Endpoint Content
requirements.text: If third-party scripts are included, the client MUST ensure that its own scripts (used to extract and remove the credentials from the URI) will execute first.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Endpoint Content
requirements.text: Instead, it SHOULD extract the credentials from the URI and redirect the user-agent again to another endpoint without exposing the credentials (in the URI or elsewhere).

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint > Endpoint Content
requirements.text: The client SHOULD NOT include any third-party scripts (e.g., third-party analytics, social plug-ins, ad networks) in the redirection endpoint response.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint
requirements.text: The endpoint URI MAY include an "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" formatted (per Appendix B) query component ([RFC3986] Section 3.4), which MUST be retained when adding additional query parameters.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint
requirements.text: The endpoint URI MUST NOT include a fragment component.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint > Redirection Endpoint
requirements.text: The redirection endpoint URI MUST be an absolute URI as defined by [RFC3986] Section 4.3.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST first verify the identity of the resource owner.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST ignore unrecognized request parameters.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST support the use of the HTTP "GET" method [RFC2616] for the authorization endpoint and MAY support the use of the "POST" method as well.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: The endpoint URI MAY include an "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" formatted (per Appendix B) query component ([RFC3986] Section 3.4), which MUST be retained when adding additional query parameters.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: The endpoint URI MUST NOT include a fragment component.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: Request and response parameters MUST NOT be included more than once.

requirements.section: Protocol Endpoints > Authorization Endpoint
requirements.text: Parameters sent without a value MUST be treated as if they were omitted from the request.

requirements.text: If the client type is confidential or the client was issued client credentials (or assigned other authentication requirements), the client MUST authenticate with the authorization server as described in Section 3.2.1.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Access Token Types
requirements.text: The client MUST NOT use an access token if it does not understand the token type.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Error Response
requirements.text: New authentication schemes MAY choose to also specify the use of the "error_description" and "error_uri" parameters to return error information in a manner parallel to their usage in this specification.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Error Response
requirements.text: Other schemes capable of being used for OAuth token authentication, but not primarily designed for that purpose, MAY bind their error values to the registry in the same manner.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Error Response
requirements.text: Such schemes MAY limit the set of valid error codes to a subset of the registered values.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Error Response
requirements.text: If the error code is returned using a named parameter, the parameter name SHOULD be "error".

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Error Response
requirements.text: New authentication schemes designed primarily for OAuth token authentication SHOULD define a mechanism for providing an error status code to the client, in which the error values allowed are registered in the error registry established by this specification.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources > Error Response
requirements.text: If a resource access request fails, the resource server SHOULD inform the client of the error.

requirements.section: Accessing Protected Resources
requirements.text: The resource server MUST validate the access token and ensure that it has not expired and that its scope covers the requested resource.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Access Token Types
requirements.text: All other types MUST be registered.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Access Token Types
requirements.text: Type names MUST conform to the type-name ABNF.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Access Token Types
requirements.text: If the type definition includes a new HTTP authentication scheme, the type name SHOULD be identical to the HTTP authentication scheme name (as defined by [RFC2617]).

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Access Token Types
requirements.text: Types utilizing a URI name SHOULD be limited to vendor-specific implementations that are not commonly applicable, and are specific to the implementation details of the resource server where they are used.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining New Endpoint Parameters
requirements.text: Parameter names MUST conform to the param-name ABNF, and parameter values syntax MUST be well-defined (e.g., using ABNF, or a reference to the syntax of an existing parameter).

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining New Endpoint Parameters
requirements.text: Unregistered vendor-specific parameter extensions that are not commonly applicable and that are specific to the implementation details of the authorization server where they are used SHOULD utilize a vendor-specific prefix that is not likely to conflict with other registered values (e.g., begin with 'companyname_').

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining New Authorization Grant Types
requirements.text: If the extension grant type requires additional token endpoint parameters, they MUST be registered in the OAuth Parameters registry as described by Section 11.2.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining New Authorization Endpoint Response Types
requirements.text: Response type names MUST conform to the response-type ABNF.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Additional Error Codes
requirements.text: In cases where protocol extensions (i.e., access token types, extension parameters, or extension grant types) require additional error codes to be used with the authorization code grant error response (Section 4.1.2.1), the implicit grant error response (Section 4.2.2.1), the token error response (Section 5.2), or the resource access error response (Section 7.2), such error codes MAY be defined.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Additional Error Codes
requirements.text: Error codes used with unregistered extensions MAY be registered.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Additional Error Codes
requirements.text: Error codes MUST conform to the error ABNF and SHOULD be prefixed by an identifying name when possible.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Additional Error Codes
requirements.text: Extension error codes MUST be registered (following the procedures in Section 11.4) if the extension they are used in conjunction with is a registered access token type, a registered endpoint parameter, or an extension grant type.

requirements.section: Extensibility > Defining Additional Error Codes
requirements.text: For example, an error identifying an invalid value set to the extension parameter "example" SHOULD be named "example_invalid".

requirements.section: Native Applications
requirements.text: Native applications that use the authorization code grant type SHOULD do so without using client credentials, due to the native application's inability to keep client credentials confidential.

requirements.section: Use of application/x-www-form-urlencoded Media Type
requirements.text: To address this shortcoming when generating payloads using this media type, names and values MUST be encoded using the UTF-8 character encoding scheme [RFC3629] first; the resulting octet sequence then needs to be further encoded using the escaping rules defined in [W3C.REC-html401-19991224].

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Authorization Request Header Field
requirements.text: Resource servers MUST support this method.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Authorization Request Header Field
requirements.text: Clients SHOULD make authenticated requests with a bearer token using the "Authorization" request header field with the "Bearer" HTTP authorization scheme.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Form-Encoded Body Parameter
requirements.text: Resource servers MAY support this method.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Form-Encoded Body Parameter
requirements.text: The content to be encoded in the entity-body MUST consist entirely of ASCII [USASCII] characters.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Form-Encoded Body Parameter
requirements.text: The entity-body MAY include other request-specific parameters, in which case the "access_token" parameter MUST be properly separated from the request-specific parameters using "&" character(s) (ASCII code 38).

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Form-Encoded Body Parameter
requirements.text: The client MUST NOT use this method unless all of the following conditions are met:

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Form-Encoded Body Parameter
requirements.text: In particular, this means that the "GET" method MUST NOT be used.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > Form-Encoded Body Parameter
requirements.text: The "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" method SHOULD NOT be used except in application contexts where participating browsers do not have access to the "Authorization" request header field.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > URI Query Parameter
requirements.text: Resource servers MAY support this method.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > URI Query Parameter
requirements.text: The HTTP request URI query can include other request-specific parameters, in which case the "access_token" parameter MUST be properly separated from the request-specific parameters using "&" character(s) (ASCII code 38).

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > URI Query Parameter
requirements.text: Clients using the URI Query Parameter method SHOULD also send a Cache-Control header containing the "no-store" option.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > URI Query Parameter
requirements.text: Because of the security weaknesses associated with the URI method (see Section 5), including the high likelihood that the URL containing the access token will be logged, it SHOULD NOT be used unless it is impossible to transport the access token in the "Authorization" request header field or the HTTP request entity-body.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests > URI Query Parameter
requirements.text: Server success (2XX status) responses to these requests SHOULD contain a Cache-Control header with the "private" option.

requirements.section: Authenticated Requests
requirements.text: Clients MUST NOT use more than one method to transmit the token in each request.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field > Error Codes
requirements.text: The client MAY request a new access token and retry the protected resource request.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field > Error Codes
requirements.text: If the request lacks any authentication information (e.g., the client was unaware that authentication is necessary or attempted using an unsupported authentication method), the resource server SHOULD NOT include an error code or other error information.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field > Error Codes
requirements.text: The resource SHOULD respond with the HTTP 401 (Unauthorized) status code.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field > Error Codes
requirements.text: The resource server SHOULD respond with the HTTP 400 (Bad Request) status code.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field > Error Codes
requirements.text: The resource server SHOULD respond with the HTTP 403 (Forbidden) status code and MAY include the "scope" attribute with the scope necessary to access the protected resource.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: In addition, the resource server MAY include the "error_description" attribute to provide developers a human-readable explanation that is not meant to be displayed to end-users.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: It also MAY include the "error_uri" attribute with an absolute URI identifying a human-readable web page explaining the error.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: Other auth-param attributes MAY be used as well.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: A "realm" attribute MAY be included to indicate the scope of protection in the manner described in HTTP/1.1 [RFC2617].

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: All challenges defined by this specification MUST use the auth-scheme value "Bearer".

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: The "error", "error_description", and "error_uri" attributes MUST NOT appear more than once.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: The "realm" attribute MUST NOT appear more than once.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: The "scope" attribute MUST NOT appear more than once.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: Values for the "error" and "error_description" attributes (specified in Appendixes A.7 and A.8 of [RFC6749]) MUST NOT include characters outside the set %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: Values for the "scope" attribute (specified in Appendix A.4 of [RFC6749]) MUST NOT include characters outside the set %x21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E for representing scope values and %x20 for delimiters between scope values.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: If the protected resource request does not include authentication credentials or does not contain an access token that enables access to the protected resource, the resource server MUST include the HTTP "WWW-Authenticate" response header field; it MAY include it in response to other conditions as well.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: This scheme MUST be followed by one or more auth-param values.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: Values for the "error_uri" attribute (specified in Appendix A.9 of [RFC6749]) MUST conform to the URI-reference syntax and thus MUST NOT include characters outside the set %x21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: Use of the "scope" attribute is OPTIONAL.

requirements.section: The WWW-Authenticate Response Header Field
requirements.text: If the protected resource request included an access token and failed authentication, the resource server SHOULD include the "error" attribute to provide the client with the reason why the access request was declined.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: The authorization server MUST implement TLS.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: For those cases where the client is prevented from observing the contents of the token, token encryption MUST be applied in addition to the usage of TLS protection.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: To deal with token capture and replay, the following recommendations are made: First, the lifetime of the token MUST be limited; one means of achieving this is by putting a validity time field inside the protected part of the token.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: In such deployments, sufficient measures MUST be employed to ensure confidentiality of the token between the front-end and back-end servers; encryption of the token is one such possible measure.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: As a further defense against token disclosure, the client MUST validate the TLS certificate chain when making requests to protected resources, including checking the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) [RFC5280].

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: Furthermore, when presenting the token to a resource server, the client MUST verify the identity of that resource server, as per Section 3.1 of "HTTP Over TLS" [RFC2818].

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: Therefore, bearer tokens MUST NOT be stored in cookies that can be sent in the clear.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: Note that the client MUST validate the TLS certificate chain when making these requests to protected resources.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: To protect against token disclosure, confidentiality protection MUST be applied using TLS [RFC5246] with a ciphersuite that provides confidentiality and integrity protection.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: Such references MUST be infeasible for an attacker to guess; using a reference may require an extra interaction between a server and the token issuer to resolve the reference to the authorization information.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: Second, confidentiality protection of the exchanges between the client and the authorization server and between the client and the resource server MUST be applied.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: The token integrity protection MUST be sufficient to prevent the token from being modified.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Threat Mitigation
requirements.text: Restricting the use of the token to a specific scope is also RECOMMENDED.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Always use TLS (https): Clients MUST always use TLS [RFC5246] (https) or equivalent transport security when making requests with bearer tokens.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Implementations that do store bearer tokens in cookies MUST take precautions against cross-site request forgery.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Don't store bearer tokens in cookies: Implementations MUST NOT store bearer tokens within cookies that can be sent in the clear (which is the default transmission mode for cookies).

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Safeguard bearer tokens: Client implementations MUST ensure that bearer tokens are not leaked to unintended parties, as they will be able to use them to gain access to protected resources.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Validate TLS certificate chains: The client MUST validate the TLS certificate chain when making requests to protected resources.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Instead, bearer tokens SHOULD be passed in HTTP message headers or message bodies for which confidentiality measures are taken.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Issue scoped bearer tokens: Token servers SHOULD issue bearer tokens that contain an audience restriction, scoping their use to the intended relying party or set of relying parties.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Issue short-lived bearer tokens: Token servers SHOULD issue short-lived (one hour or less) bearer tokens, particularly when issuing tokens to clients that run within a web browser or other environments where information leakage may occur.

requirements.section: Security Considerations > Summary of Recommendations
requirements.text: Don't pass bearer tokens in page URLs: Bearer tokens SHOULD NOT be passed in page URLs (for example, as query string parameters).

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > "Boundary" Parameter of multipart/form-data
requirements.text: As noted in Section 5.1 of [RFC2046], the boundary delimiter MUST NOT appear inside any of the encapsulated parts, and it is often necessary to enclose the "boundary" parameter values in quotes in the Content-Type header field.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Disposition Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: In most multipart types, the MIME header fields in each part are restricted to US-ASCII; for compatibility with those systems, file names normally visible to users MAY be encoded using the percent-encoding method in Section 2, following how a "file:" URI [URI-SCHEME] might be encoded.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Disposition Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: The Content-Disposition header field MUST also contain an additional parameter of "name"; the value of the "name" parameter is the original field name from the form (possibly encoded; see Section 5.1).

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Disposition Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: Each part MUST contain a Content-Disposition header field [RFC2183] where the disposition type is "form-data".

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Disposition Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: NOTE: The encoding method described in [RFC5987], which would add a "filename*" parameter to the Content-Disposition header field, MUST NOT be used.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Disposition Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: For form data that represents the content of a file, a name for the file SHOULD be supplied as well, by using a "filename" parameter of the Content-Disposition header field.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Multiple Files for One Form Field
requirements.text: To match widely deployed implementations, multiple files MUST be sent by supplying each file in a separate part but all with the same "name" parameter.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Multiple Files for One Form Field
requirements.text: Receiving applications intended for wide applicability (e.g., multipart/form-data parsing libraries) SHOULD also support the older method of supplying multiple files.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Type Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: Each part MAY have an (optional) "Content-Type" header field, which defaults to "text/plain".

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Type Header Field for Each Part
requirements.text: If the contents of a file are to be sent, the file data SHOULD be labeled with an appropriate media type, if known, or "application/octet-stream".

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > The Charset Parameter for "text/plain" Form Data
requirements.text: In the case where the form data is text, the charset parameter for the "text/plain" Content-Type MAY be used to indicate the character encoding used in that part.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Content-Transfer-Encoding Deprecated
requirements.text: Senders SHOULD NOT generate any parts with a Content-Transfer-Encoding header field.

requirements.section: Definition of multipart/form-data > Other "Content-" Header Fields
requirements.text: Other header fields MUST NOT be included and MUST be ignored.

requirements.section: Operability Considerations > Non-ASCII Field Names and Values > Avoid Non-ASCII Field Names
requirements.text: For broadest interoperability with existing deployed software, those creating forms SHOULD avoid non-ASCII field names.

requirements.section: Operability Considerations > Non-ASCII Field Names and Values > Avoid Non-ASCII Field Names
requirements.text: If non-ASCII field names are unavoidable, form or application creators SHOULD use UTF-8 uniformly.

requirements.section: Operability Considerations > Non-ASCII Field Names and Values > Interpreting Forms and Creating multipart/form-data Data
requirements.text: Any text, whether field name, field value, or ("text/plain") form data that uses characters outside the ASCII range MAY be represented directly encoded in the form-charset.

requirements.section: Operability Considerations > Ordered Fields and Duplicated Field Names
requirements.text: Form parts with identical field names MUST NOT be coalesced.

requirements.section: Operability Considerations > Ordered Fields and Duplicated Field Names
requirements.text: Intermediaries MUST NOT reorder the results.

requirements.section: Operability Considerations > Ordered Fields and Duplicated Field Names
requirements.text: Form processors given forms with a well-defined ordering SHOULD send back results in order.

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme > The 'charset' auth-param
requirements.text: For the password, recipients MUST support all characters defined in the "OpaqueString" profile defined in Section 4.2 of [RFC7613].

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme > The 'charset' auth-param
requirements.text: For the user-id, recipients MUST support all characters defined in the "UsernameCasePreserved" profile defined in Section 3.3 of [RFC7613], with the exception of the colon (":") character.

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme > Reusing Credentials
requirements.text: A client MAY preemptively send the corresponding Authorization header field with requests for resources in that space without receipt of another challenge from the server.

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme > Reusing Credentials
requirements.text: Similarly, when a client sends a request to a proxy, it MAY reuse a user-id and password in the Proxy-Authorization header field without receiving another challenge from the proxy server.

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme > Reusing Credentials
requirements.text: A client SHOULD assume that resources identified by URIs with a prefix-match of the authentication scope are also within the protection space specified by the realm value of that authenticated request.

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme
requirements.text: No other authentication parameters are defined -- unknown parameters MUST be ignored by recipients, and new parameters can only be defined by revising this specification.

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme
requirements.text: The user-id and password MUST NOT contain any control characters (see "CTL" in Appendix B.1 of [RFC5234]).

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme
requirements.text: The authentication parameter 'charset' is OPTIONAL (see Section 2.1).

requirements.section: The 'Basic' Authentication Scheme
requirements.text: The authentication parameter 'realm' is REQUIRED ([RFC7235], Section 2.2).

requirements.section: Security Considerations
requirements.text: Because Basic authentication involves the cleartext transmission of passwords, it SHOULD NOT be used (without enhancements such as HTTPS [RFC2818]) to protect sensitive or valuable information.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A client that sends a 100-continue expectation is not required to wait for any specific length of time; such a client MAY proceed to send the content even if it has not yet received a response.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: If the proxy believes (from configuration or past interaction) that the next inbound server only supports HTTP/1.0, the proxy MAY generate an immediate 100 (Continue) response to encourage the client to begin sending the content.
