requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A server MAY omit sending a 100 (Continue) response if it has already received some or all of the content for the corresponding request, or if the framing indicates that there is no content.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A server that receives an Expect field value containing a member other than 100-continue MAY respond with a 417 (Expectation Failed) status code to indicate that the unexpected expectation cannot be met.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A client that will wait for a 100 (Continue) response before sending the request content MUST send an Expect header field containing a 100-continue expectation.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A client MUST NOT generate a 100-continue expectation in a request that does not include content.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: The origin server MUST NOT wait for the content before sending the 100 (Continue) response.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A server that receives a 100-continue expectation in an HTTP/1.0 request MUST ignore that expectation.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A server that sends a 100 (Continue) response MUST ultimately send a final status code, once it receives and processes the request content, unless the connection is closed prematurely.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: Upon receiving an HTTP/1.1 (or later) request that has a method, target URI, and complete header section that contains a 100-continue expectation and an indication that request content will follow, an origin server MUST send either:

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: Upon receiving an HTTP/1.1 (or later) request that has a method, target URI, and complete header section that contains a 100-continue expectation and indicates a request content will follow, a proxy MUST either:

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A client that receives a 417 (Expectation Failed) status code in response to a request containing a 100-continue expectation SHOULD repeat that request without a 100-continue expectation, since the 417 response merely indicates that the response chain does not support expectations (e.g., it passes through an HTTP/1.0 server).

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: Furthermore, since 100 (Continue) responses cannot be sent through an HTTP/1.0 intermediary, such a client SHOULD NOT wait for an indefinite period before sending the content.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Expect
requirements.text: A server that responds with a final status code before reading the entire request content SHOULD indicate whether it intends to close the connection (e.g., see Section 9.6 of [HTTP/1.1]) or continue reading the request content.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > From
requirements.text: A server SHOULD NOT use the From header field for access control or authentication, since its value is expected to be visible to anyone receiving or observing the request and is often recorded within logfiles and error reports without any expectation of privacy.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > From
requirements.text: A user agent SHOULD NOT send a From header field without explicit configuration by the user, since that might conflict with the user's privacy interests or their site's security policy.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > From
requirements.text: A robotic user agent SHOULD send a valid From header field so that the person responsible for running the robot can be contacted if problems occur on servers, such as if the robot is sending excessive, unwanted, or invalid requests.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Referer
requirements.text: The Referer header field value need not convey the full URI of the referring resource; a user agent MAY truncate parts other than the referring origin.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Referer
requirements.text: A user agent MUST NOT include the fragment and userinfo components of the URI reference [URI], if any, when generating the Referer field value.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Referer
requirements.text: A user agent MUST NOT send a Referer header field in an unsecured HTTP request if the referring resource was accessed with a secure protocol.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Referer
requirements.text: If the target URI was obtained from a source that does not have its own URI (e.g., input from the user keyboard, or an entry within the user's bookmarks/favorites), the user agent MUST either exclude the Referer header field or send it with a value of "about:blank".

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Referer
requirements.text: An intermediary SHOULD NOT modify or delete the Referer header field when the field value shares the same scheme and host as the target URI.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > Referer
requirements.text: A user agent SHOULD NOT send a Referer header field if the referring resource was accessed with a secure protocol and the request target has an origin differing from that of the referring resource, unless the referring resource explicitly allows Referer to be sent.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > TE
requirements.text: A sender of TE MUST also send a "TE" connection option within the Connection header field (Section 7.6.1) to inform intermediaries not to forward this field.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > User-Agent
requirements.text: A sender SHOULD limit generated product identifiers to what is necessary to identify the product; a sender MUST NOT generate advertising or other nonessential information within the product identifier.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > User-Agent
requirements.text: A sender SHOULD NOT generate information in product-version that is not a version identifier (i.e., successive versions of the same product name ought to differ only in the product-version portion of the product identifier).

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > User-Agent
requirements.text: A user agent SHOULD NOT generate a User-Agent header field containing needlessly fine-grained detail and SHOULD limit the addition of subproducts by third parties.

requirements.section: Message Context > Request Context Fields > User-Agent
requirements.text: A user agent SHOULD send a User-Agent header field in each request unless specifically configured not to do so.

requirements.section: Message Context > Response Context Fields > Allow
requirements.text: A proxy MUST NOT modify the Allow header field -- it does not need to understand all of the indicated methods in order to handle them according to the generic message handling rules.

requirements.section: Message Context > Response Context Fields > Allow
requirements.text: An origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405 (Method Not Allowed) response and MAY do so in any other response.

requirements.section: Message Context > Response Context Fields > Location
requirements.text: If the Location value provided in a 3xx (Redirection) response does not have a fragment component, a user agent MUST process the redirection as if the value inherits the fragment component of the URI reference used to generate the target URI (i.e., the redirection inherits the original reference's fragment, if any).

requirements.section: Message Context > Response Context Fields > Server
requirements.text: An origin server MAY generate a Server header field in its responses.

requirements.section: Message Context > Response Context Fields > Server
requirements.text: An origin server SHOULD NOT generate a Server header field containing needlessly fine-grained detail and SHOULD limit the addition of subproducts by third parties.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authentication Parameters
requirements.text: Authentication parameters are name/value pairs, where the name token is matched case-insensitively and each parameter name MUST only occur once per challenge.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Credentials
requirements.text: Likewise, upon receipt of a request that omits proxy credentials or contains invalid or partial proxy credentials, a proxy that requires authentication SHOULD generate a 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response that contains a Proxy-Authenticate header field with at least one (possibly new) challenge applicable to the proxy.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Credentials
requirements.text: Upon receipt of a request for a protected resource that omits credentials, contains invalid credentials (e.g., a bad password) or partial credentials (e.g., when the authentication scheme requires more than one round trip), an origin server SHOULD send a 401 (Unauthorized) response that contains a WWW-Authenticate header field with at least one (possibly new) challenge applicable to the requested resource.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
requirements.text: If a prior request has been authorized, the user agent MAY reuse the same credentials for all other requests within that protection space for a period of time determined by the authentication scheme, parameters, and/or user preferences (such as a configurable inactivity timeout).

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Establishing a Protection Space (Realm)
requirements.text: For historical reasons, a sender MUST only generate the quoted-string syntax.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authenticating Users to Origin Servers > WWW-Authenticate
requirements.text: A server MAY generate a WWW-Authenticate header field in other response messages to indicate that supplying credentials (or different credentials) might affect the response.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authenticating Users to Origin Servers > WWW-Authenticate
requirements.text: A proxy forwarding a response MUST NOT modify any WWW-Authenticate header fields in that response.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authenticating Users to Origin Servers > WWW-Authenticate
requirements.text: A server generating a 401 (Unauthorized) response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field containing at least one challenge.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authenticating Users to Origin Servers > Authorization
requirements.text: A proxy forwarding a request MUST NOT modify any Authorization header fields in that request.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authenticating Clients to Proxies > Proxy-Authenticate
requirements.text: A proxy MUST send at least one Proxy-Authenticate header field in each 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response that it generates.

requirements.section: HTTP Authentication > Authenticating Clients to Proxies > Proxy-Authorization
requirements.text: A proxy MAY relay the credentials from the client request to the next proxy if that is the mechanism by which the proxies cooperatively authenticate a given request.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Proactive Negotiation
requirements.text: In order to improve the server's guess, a user agent MAY send request header fields that describe its preferences.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Field Features > Quality Values
requirements.text: A sender of qvalue MUST NOT generate more than three digits after the decimal point.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept
requirements.text: Recipients SHOULD process any parameter named "q" as weight, regardless of parameter ordering.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept
requirements.text: Senders using weights SHOULD send "q" last (after all media-range parameters).

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept-Charset
requirements.text: A user agent MAY associate a quality value with each charset to indicate the user's relative preference for that charset, as defined in Section 12.4.2.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept-Encoding
requirements.text: Each codings value MAY be given an associated quality value (weight) representing the preference for that encoding, as defined in Section 12.4.2.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept-Encoding
requirements.text: In order to avoid confusion with issues related to media types, servers that fail a request with a 415 status for reasons unrelated to content codings MUST NOT include the Accept-Encoding header field.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept-Encoding
requirements.text: If a non-empty Accept-Encoding header field is present in a request and none of the available representations for the response have a content coding that is listed as acceptable, the origin server SHOULD send a response without any content coding unless the identity coding is indicated as unacceptable.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Accept-Language
requirements.text: A user agent that does not provide such control to the user MUST NOT send an Accept-Language header field.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Vary
requirements.text: To inform cache recipients that they MUST NOT use this response to satisfy a later request unless the later request has the same values for the listed header fields as the original request (Section 4.1 of [CACHING]) or reuse of the response has been validated by the origin server.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Vary
requirements.text: A proxy MUST NOT generate "*" in a Vary field value.

requirements.section: Content Negotiation > Content Negotiation Fields > Vary
requirements.text: An origin server SHOULD generate a Vary header field on a cacheable response when it wishes that response to be selectively reused for subsequent requests.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: Alternatively, if the request is a state-changing operation that appears to have already been applied to the selected representation, the origin server MAY respond with a 2xx (Successful) status code (i.e., the change requested by the user agent has already succeeded, but the user agent might not be aware of it, perhaps because the prior response was lost or an equivalent change was made by some other user agent).

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: A cache or intermediary MAY ignore If-Match because its interoperability features are only necessary for an origin server.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: A client MAY send an If-Match header field in a GET request to indicate that it would prefer a 412 (Precondition Failed) response if the selected representation does not match.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: Instead, the origin server MAY indicate that the conditional request failed by responding with a 412 (Precondition Failed) status code.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: An origin server that evaluates an If-Match condition MUST NOT perform the requested method if the condition evaluates to false.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: When an origin server receives a request that selects a representation and that request includes an If-Match header field, the origin server MUST evaluate the If-Match condition per Section 13.2 prior to performing the method.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Match
requirements.text: An origin server MUST use the strong comparison function when comparing entity tags for If-Match (Section 8.8.3.2), since the client intends this precondition to prevent the method from being applied if there have been any changes to the representation data.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-None-Match
requirements.text: An origin server that evaluates an If-None-Match condition MUST NOT perform the requested method if the condition evaluates to false; instead, the origin server MUST respond with either a) the 304 (Not Modified) status code if the request method is GET or HEAD or b) the 412 (Precondition Failed) status code for all other request methods.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-None-Match
requirements.text: When an origin server receives a request that selects a representation and that request includes an If-None-Match header field, the origin server MUST evaluate the If-None-Match condition per Section 13.2 prior to performing the method.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-None-Match
requirements.text: A recipient MUST use the weak comparison function when comparing entity tags for If-None-Match (Section 8.8.3.2), since weak entity tags can be used for cache validation even if there have been changes to the representation data.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-None-Match
requirements.text: When a client desires to update one or more stored responses that have entity tags, the client SHOULD generate an If-None-Match header field containing a list of those entity tags when making a GET request; this allows recipient servers to send a 304 (Not Modified) response to indicate when one of those stored responses matches the selected representation.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Modified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST ignore the If-Modified-Since header field if the received field value is not a valid HTTP-date, the field value has more than one member, or if the request method is neither GET nor HEAD.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Modified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST ignore the If-Modified-Since header field if the resource does not have a modification date available.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Modified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST ignore If-Modified-Since if the request contains an If-None-Match header field; the condition in If-None-Match is considered to be a more accurate replacement for the condition in If-Modified-Since, and the two are only combined for the sake of interoperating with older intermediaries that might not implement If-None-Match.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Modified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST interpret an If-Modified-Since field value's timestamp in terms of the origin server's clock.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Modified-Since
requirements.text: An origin server that evaluates an If-Modified-Since condition SHOULD NOT perform the requested method if the condition evaluates to false; instead, the origin server SHOULD generate a 304 (Not Modified) response, including only those metadata that are useful for identifying or updating a previously cached response.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Modified-Since
requirements.text: When an origin server receives a request that selects a representation and that request includes an If-Modified-Since header field without an If-None-Match header field, the origin server SHOULD evaluate the If-Modified-Since condition per Section 13.2 prior to performing the method.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: Alternatively, if the request is a state-changing operation that appears to have already been applied to the selected representation, the origin server MAY respond with a 2xx (Successful) status code (i.e., the change requested by the user agent has already succeeded, but the user agent might not be aware of it, perhaps because the prior response was lost or an equivalent change was made by some other user agent).

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: A cache or intermediary MAY ignore If-Unmodified-Since because its interoperability features are only necessary for an origin server.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: A client MAY send an If-Unmodified-Since header field in a GET request to indicate that it would prefer a 412 (Precondition Failed) response if the selected representation has been modified.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: Instead, the origin server MAY indicate that the conditional request failed by responding with a 412 (Precondition Failed) status code.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: An origin server that evaluates an If-Unmodified-Since condition MUST NOT perform the requested method if the condition evaluates to false.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: When an origin server receives a request that selects a representation and that request includes an If-Unmodified-Since header field without an If-Match header field, the origin server MUST evaluate the If-Unmodified-Since condition per Section 13.2 prior to performing the method.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST ignore the If-Unmodified-Since header field if the received field value is not a valid HTTP-date (including when the field value appears to be a list of dates).

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST ignore the If-Unmodified-Since header field if the resource does not have a modification date available.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST ignore If-Unmodified-Since if the request contains an If-Match header field; the condition in If-Match is considered to be a more accurate replacement for the condition in If-Unmodified-Since, and the two are only combined for the sake of interoperating with older intermediaries that might not implement If-Match.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Unmodified-Since
requirements.text: A recipient MUST interpret an If-Unmodified-Since field value's timestamp in terms of the origin server's clock.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: A client MUST NOT generate an If-Range header field containing an entity tag that is marked as weak.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: A client MUST NOT generate an If-Range header field containing an HTTP-date unless the client has no entity tag for the corresponding representation and the date is a strong validator in the sense defined by Section 8.8.2.2.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: A client MUST NOT generate an If-Range header field in a request that does not contain a Range header field.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: An origin server MUST ignore an If-Range header field received in a request for a target resource that does not support Range requests.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: A recipient of an If-Range header field MUST ignore the Range header field if the If-Range condition evaluates to false.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: A server MUST ignore an If-Range header field received in a request that does not contain a Range header field.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: A server that receives an If-Range header field on a Range request MUST evaluate the condition per Section 13.2 prior to performing the method.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Preconditions > If-Range
requirements.text: Otherwise, the recipient SHOULD process the Range header field as requested.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Evaluation of Preconditions > When to Evaluate
requirements.text: Except when excluded below, a recipient cache or origin server MUST evaluate received request preconditions after it has successfully performed its normal request checks and just before it would process the request content (if any) or perform the action associated with the request method.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Evaluation of Preconditions > When to Evaluate
requirements.text: Likewise, a server MUST ignore the conditional request header fields defined by this specification when received with a request method that does not involve the selection or modification of a selected representation, such as CONNECT, OPTIONS, or TRACE.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Evaluation of Preconditions > When to Evaluate
requirements.text: A server that is not the origin server for the target resource and cannot act as a cache for requests on the target resource MUST NOT evaluate the conditional request header fields defined by this specification, and it MUST forward them if the request is forwarded, since the generating client intends that they be evaluated by a server that can provide a current representation.

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Evaluation of Preconditions > When to Evaluate
requirements.text: A server MUST ignore all received preconditions if its response to the same request without those conditions, prior to processing the request content, would have been a status code other than a 2xx (Successful) or 412 (Precondition Failed).

requirements.section: Conditional Requests > Evaluation of Preconditions > Precedence of Preconditions
requirements.text: A recipient cache or origin server MUST evaluate the request preconditions defined by this specification in the following order:

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range Units > Byte Ranges
requirements.text: Since there is no predefined limit to the length of content, recipients MUST anticipate potentially large decimal numerals and prevent parsing errors due to integer conversion overflows.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A proxy MAY discard a Range header field that contains a range unit it does not understand.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A server MAY ignore the Range header field.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A server that supports range requests MAY ignore a Range header field when the selected representation has no content (i.e., the selected representation's data is of zero length).

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A server that supports range requests MAY ignore or reject a Range header field that contains an invalid ranges-specifier (Section 14.1.1), a ranges-specifier with more than two overlapping ranges, or a set of many small ranges that are not listed in ascending order, since these are indications of either a broken client or a deliberate denial-of-service attack (Section 17.15).

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: An origin server MUST ignore a Range header field that contains a range unit it does not understand.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A server MUST ignore a Range header field received with a request method that is unrecognized or for which range handling is not defined.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: If all of the preconditions are true, the server supports the Range header field for the target resource, the received Range field-value contains a valid ranges-specifier with a range-unit supported for that target resource, and that ranges-specifier is satisfiable with respect to the selected representation, the server SHOULD send a 206 (Partial Content) response with content containing one or more partial representations that correspond to the satisfiable range-spec(s) requested.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: If all of the preconditions are true, the server supports the Range header field for the target resource, the received Range field-value contains a valid ranges-specifier, and either the range-unit is not supported for that target resource or the ranges-specifier is unsatisfiable with respect to the selected representation, the server SHOULD send a 416 (Range Not Satisfiable) response.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A client that is requesting multiple ranges SHOULD list those ranges in ascending order (the order in which they would typically be received in a complete representation) unless there is a specific need to request a later part earlier.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Range
requirements.text: A client SHOULD NOT request multiple ranges that are inherently less efficient to process and transfer than a single range that encompasses the same data.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Accept-Ranges
requirements.text: The Accept-Ranges field MAY be sent in a trailer section, but is preferred to be sent as a header field because the information is particularly useful for restarting large information transfers that have failed in mid-content (before the trailer section is received).

requirements.section: Range Requests > Accept-Ranges
requirements.text: A client MAY generate range requests regardless of having received an Accept-Ranges field.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Accept-Ranges
requirements.text: A server that does not support any kind of range request for the target resource MAY send

requirements.section: Range Requests > Accept-Ranges
requirements.text: Conversely, a client MUST NOT assume that receiving an Accept-Ranges field means that future range requests will return partial responses.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Content-Range
requirements.text: If a 206 (Partial Content) response contains a Content-Range header field with a range unit (Section 14.1) that the recipient does not understand, the recipient MUST NOT attempt to recombine it with a stored representation.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Content-Range
requirements.text: The recipient of an invalid Content-Range MUST NOT attempt to recombine the received content with a stored representation.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Content-Range
requirements.text: A server MUST ignore a Content-Range header field received in a request with a method for which Content-Range support is not defined.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Content-Range
requirements.text: For byte ranges, a sender SHOULD indicate the complete length of the representation from which the range has been extracted, unless the complete length is unknown or difficult to determine.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Content-Range
requirements.text: A proxy that receives such a message SHOULD forward it downstream.

requirements.section: Range Requests > Content-Range
requirements.text: A server generating a 416 (Range Not Satisfiable) response to a byte-range request SHOULD send a Content-Range header field with an unsatisfied-range value, as in the following example:

requirements.section: Range Requests > Partial PUT
requirements.text: An origin server SHOULD respond with a 400 (Bad Request) status code if it receives Content-Range on a PUT for a target resource that does not support partial PUT requests.

requirements.section: Range Requests
requirements.text: Range requests are an OPTIONAL feature of HTTP, designed so that recipients not implementing this feature (or not supporting it for the target resource) can respond as if it is a normal GET request without impacting interoperability.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Informational 1xx > 101 Switching Protocols
requirements.text: The server MUST generate an Upgrade header field in the response that indicates which protocol(s) will be in effect after this response.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Informational 1xx
requirements.text: A user agent MAY ignore unexpected 1xx responses.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Informational 1xx
requirements.text: A client MUST be able to parse one or more 1xx responses received prior to a final response, even if the client does not expect one.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Informational 1xx
requirements.text: Since HTTP/1.0 did not define any 1xx status codes, a server MUST NOT send a 1xx response to an HTTP/1.0 client.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Informational 1xx
requirements.text: A proxy MUST forward 1xx responses unless the proxy itself requested the generation of the 1xx response.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 200 OK
requirements.text: In 200 responses to GET or HEAD, an origin server SHOULD send any available validator fields (Section 8.8) for the selected representation, with both a strong entity tag and a Last-Modified date being preferred.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 205 Reset Content
requirements.text: Since the 205 status code implies that no additional content will be provided, a server MUST NOT generate content in a 205 response.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Single Part
requirements.text: If a single part is being transferred, the server generating the 206 response MUST generate a Content-Range header field, describing what range of the selected representation is enclosed, and a content consisting of the range.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: However, a server MAY generate a "multipart/byteranges" response with only a single body part if multiple ranges were requested and only one range was found to be satisfiable or only one range remained after coalescing.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: When multiple ranges are requested, a server MAY coalesce any of the ranges that overlap, or that are separated by a gap that is smaller than the overhead of sending multiple parts, regardless of the order in which the corresponding range-spec appeared in the received Range header field.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: A client that receives a multipart response MUST inspect the Content-Range header field present in each body part in order to determine which range is contained in that body part; a client cannot rely on receiving the same ranges that it requested, nor the same order that it requested.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: If multiple parts are being transferred, the server generating the 206 response MUST generate "multipart/byteranges" content, as defined in Section 14.6, and a Content-Type header field containing the "multipart/byteranges" media type and its required boundary parameter.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: To avoid confusion with single-part responses, a server MUST NOT generate a Content-Range header field in the HTTP header section of a multiple part response (this field will be sent in each part instead).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: A client that cannot process a "multipart/byteranges" response MUST NOT generate a request that asks for multiple ranges.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: A server MUST NOT generate a multipart response to a request for a single range, since a client that does not request multiple parts might not support multipart responses.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: Within the header area of each body part in the multipart content, the server MUST generate a Content-Range header field corresponding to the range being enclosed in that body part.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: If the selected representation would have had a Content-Type header field in a 200 (OK) response, the server SHOULD generate that same Content-Type header field in the header area of each body part.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Multiple Parts
requirements.text: A server that generates a multipart response SHOULD send the parts in the same order that the corresponding range-spec appeared in the received Range header field, excluding those ranges that were deemed unsatisfiable or that were coalesced into other ranges.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Combining Parts
requirements.text: A client that has received multiple partial responses to GET requests on a target resource MAY combine those responses into a larger continuous range if they share the same strong validator.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Combining Parts
requirements.text: If all of the matching stored responses are 206 responses, then the stored response with the most recent header fields is used as the source of header fields for the combined response, except that the client MUST use other header fields provided in the new response, aside from Content-Range, to replace all instances of the corresponding header fields in the stored response.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Combining Parts
requirements.text: Otherwise, the client MUST process the set of continuous ranges as one of the following: an incomplete 200 (OK) response if the combined response is a prefix of the representation, a single 206 (Partial Content) response containing "multipart/byteranges" content, or multiple 206 (Partial Content) responses, each with one continuous range that is indicated by a Content-Range header field.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content > Combining Parts
requirements.text: If the union consists of the entire range of the representation, then the client MUST process the combined response as if it were a complete 200 (OK) response, including a Content-Length header field that reflects the complete length.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content
requirements.text: A client MUST inspect a 206 response's Content-Type and Content-Range field(s) to determine what parts are enclosed and whether additional requests are needed.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content
requirements.text: Otherwise, a sender MUST generate all of the representation header fields that would have been sent in a 200 (OK) response to the same request.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content
requirements.text: A server that generates a 206 response MUST generate the following header fields, in addition to those required in the subsections below, if the field would have been sent in a 200 (OK) response to the same request: Date, Cache-Control, ETag, Expires, Content-Location, and Vary.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Successful 2xx > 206 Partial Content
requirements.text: A sender that generates a 206 response to a request with an If-Range header field SHOULD NOT generate other representation header fields beyond those required because the client already has a prior response containing those header fields.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 300 Multiple Choices
requirements.text: The user agent MAY make a selection from that list automatically if it understands the provided media type.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 300 Multiple Choices
requirements.text: The user agent MAY use the Location field value for automatic redirection.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 300 Multiple Choices
requirements.text: For request methods other than HEAD, the server SHOULD generate content in the 300 response containing a list of representation metadata and URI reference(s) from which the user or user agent can choose the one most preferred.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 300 Multiple Choices
requirements.text: If the server has a preferred choice, the server SHOULD generate a Location header field containing a preferred choice's URI reference.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 301 Moved Permanently
requirements.text: Note: For historical reasons, a user agent MAY change the request method from POST to GET for the subsequent request.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 301 Moved Permanently
requirements.text: The user agent MAY use the Location field value for automatic redirection.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 301 Moved Permanently
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate a Location header field in the response containing a preferred URI reference for the new permanent URI.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 302 Found
requirements.text: Note: For historical reasons, a user agent MAY change the request method from POST to GET for the subsequent request.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 302 Found
requirements.text: The user agent MAY use the Location field value for automatic redirection.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 302 Found
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate a Location header field in the response containing a URI reference for the different URI.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 304 Not Modified
requirements.text: The server generating a 304 response MUST generate any of the following header fields that would have been sent in a 200 (OK) response to the same request:

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 304 Not Modified
requirements.text: If the conditional request originated with an outbound client, such as a user agent with its own cache sending a conditional GET to a shared proxy, then the proxy SHOULD forward the 304 response to that client.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 304 Not Modified
requirements.text: Since the goal of a 304 response is to minimize information transfer when the recipient already has one or more cached representations, a sender SHOULD NOT generate representation metadata other than the above listed fields unless said metadata exists for the purpose of guiding cache updates (e.g., Last-Modified might be useful if the response does not have an ETag field).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 307 Temporary Redirect
requirements.text: The user agent MAY use the Location field value for automatic redirection.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 307 Temporary Redirect
requirements.text: The 307 (Temporary Redirect) status code indicates that the target resource resides temporarily under a different URI and the user agent MUST NOT change the request method if it performs an automatic redirection to that URI.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 307 Temporary Redirect
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate a Location header field in the response containing a URI reference for the different URI.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 308 Permanent Redirect
requirements.text: The user agent MAY use the Location field value for automatic redirection.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx > 308 Permanent Redirect
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate a Location header field in the response containing a preferred URI reference for the new permanent URI.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx
requirements.text: If a Location header field (Section 10.2.2) is provided, the user agent MAY automatically redirect its request to the URI referenced by the Location field value, even if the specific status code is not understood.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx
requirements.text: When automatically following a redirected request, the user agent SHOULD resend the original request message with the following modifications:

requirements.section: Status Codes > Redirection 3xx
requirements.text: A client SHOULD detect and intervene in cyclical redirections (i.e., "infinite" redirection loops).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 409 Conflict
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate content that includes enough information for a user to recognize the source of the conflict.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 411 Length Required
requirements.text: The client MAY repeat the request if it adds a valid Content-Length header field containing the length of the request content.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 413 Content Too Large
requirements.text: The server MAY terminate the request, if the protocol version in use allows it; otherwise, the server MAY close the connection.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 413 Content Too Large
requirements.text: If the condition is temporary, the server SHOULD generate a Retry-After header field to indicate that it is temporary and after what time the client MAY try again.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 416 Range Not Satisfiable
requirements.text: A server that generates a 416 response to a byte-range request SHOULD generate a Content-Range header field specifying the current length of the selected representation (Section 14.4).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 401 Unauthorized
requirements.text: The user agent MAY repeat the request with a new or replaced Authorization header field (Section 11.6.2).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 401 Unauthorized
requirements.text: The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field (Section 11.6.1) containing at least one challenge applicable to the target resource.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 401 Unauthorized
requirements.text: If the 401 response contains the same challenge as the prior response, and the user agent has already attempted authentication at least once, then the user agent SHOULD present the enclosed representation to the user, since it usually contains relevant diagnostic information.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 421 Misdirected Request
requirements.text: A client that receives a 421 (Misdirected Request) response MAY retry the request, whether or not the request method is idempotent, over a different connection, such as a fresh connection specific to the target resource's origin, or via an alternative service [ALTSVC].

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 421 Misdirected Request
requirements.text: A proxy MUST NOT generate a 421 response.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 426 Upgrade Required
requirements.text: The server MUST send an Upgrade header field in a 426 response to indicate the required protocol(s) (Section 7.8).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 403 Forbidden
requirements.text: The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 403 Forbidden
requirements.text: An origin server that wishes to "hide" the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 403 Forbidden
requirements.text: The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 405 Method Not Allowed
requirements.text: The origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405 response containing a list of the target resource's currently supported methods.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 406 Not Acceptable
requirements.text: A user agent MAY automatically select the most appropriate choice from that list.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 406 Not Acceptable
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate content containing a list of available representation characteristics and corresponding resource identifiers from which the user or user agent can choose the one most appropriate.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 407 Proxy Authentication Required
requirements.text: The client MAY repeat the request with a new or replaced Proxy-Authorization header field (Section 11.7.2).

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 407 Proxy Authentication Required
requirements.text: The proxy MUST send a Proxy-Authenticate header field (Section 11.7.1) containing a challenge applicable to that proxy for the request.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx > 408 Request Timeout
requirements.text: If the client has an outstanding request in transit, it MAY repeat that request.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx
requirements.text: Except when responding to a HEAD request, the server SHOULD send a representation containing an explanation of the error situation, and whether it is a temporary or permanent condition.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Client Error 4xx
requirements.text: User agents SHOULD display any included representation to the user.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Server Error 5xx > 503 Service Unavailable
requirements.text: The server MAY send a Retry-After header field (Section 10.2.3) to suggest an appropriate amount of time for the client to wait before retrying the request.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Server Error 5xx > 505 HTTP Version Not Supported
requirements.text: The server SHOULD generate a representation for the 505 response that describes why that version is not supported and what other protocols are supported by that server.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Server Error 5xx
requirements.text: Except when responding to a HEAD request, the server SHOULD send a representation containing an explanation of the error situation, and whether it is a temporary or permanent condition.

requirements.section: Status Codes > Server Error 5xx
requirements.text: A user agent SHOULD display any included representation to the user.

requirements.section: Status Codes
requirements.text: However, a client MUST understand the class of any status code, as indicated by the first digit, and treat an unrecognized status code as being equivalent to the x00 status code of that class.

requirements.section: Status Codes
requirements.text: A client that receives a response with an invalid status code SHOULD process the response as if it had a 5xx (Server Error) status code.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Method Extensibility > Method Registry
requirements.text: HTTP method registrations MUST include the following fields:

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Status Code Extensibility > Status Code Registry
requirements.text: A registration MUST include the following fields:

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Field Extensibility > Field Name Registry
requirements.text: It MUST conform to the field-name syntax defined in Section 5.1, and it SHOULD be restricted to just letters, digits, and hyphen ('-') characters, with the first character being a letter.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Field Extensibility > Considerations for New Fields > Considerations for New Field Names
requirements.text: To be interoperable, new field names SHOULD constrain themselves to alphanumeric characters, "-", and ".", and SHOULD begin with a letter.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Authentication Scheme Extensibility > Authentication Scheme Registry
requirements.text: Registrations MUST include the following fields:

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Authentication Scheme Extensibility > Considerations for New Authentication Schemes
requirements.text: HTTP authentication is presumed to be stateless: all of the information necessary to authenticate a request MUST be provided in the request, rather than be dependent on the server remembering prior requests.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Authentication Scheme Extensibility > Considerations for New Authentication Schemes
requirements.text: New schemes MUST NOT use it in a way incompatible with that definition.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Range Unit Extensibility > Range Unit Registry
requirements.text: Registration of an HTTP Range Unit MUST include the following fields:

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Content Coding Extensibility > Content Coding Registry
requirements.text: Content coding registrations MUST include the following fields:

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Content Coding Extensibility > Content Coding Registry
requirements.text: Names of content codings MUST NOT overlap with names of transfer codings (per the "HTTP Transfer Coding Registry" located at ) unless the encoding transformation is identical (as is the case for the compression codings defined in Section 8.4.1).

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Content Coding Extensibility > Content Coding Registry
requirements.text: Values to be added to this namespace require IETF Review (see Section 4.8 of [RFC8126]) and MUST conform to the purpose of content coding defined in Section 8.4.1.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Upgrade Token Registry
requirements.text: The IESG MAY reassign responsibility for a protocol token.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Upgrade Token Registry
requirements.text: The registration MAY name a set of specifications associated with that token.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Upgrade Token Registry
requirements.text: The responsible party MAY change the registration at any time.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Upgrade Token Registry
requirements.text: The registration MUST name a point of contact.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Upgrade Token Registry
requirements.text: The registration MUST name a responsible party for the registration.

requirements.section: Extending HTTP > Upgrade Token Registry
requirements.text: The registration SHOULD name a set of expected "protocol-version" tokens associated with that token at the time of registration.

requirements.section: Conformance > Requirements Notation
requirements.text: A recipient MAY employ such workarounds while remaining conformant to this protocol if the workarounds are limited to the implementations at fault.

requirements.section: Conformance > Requirements Notation
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate protocol elements that do not match the grammar defined by the corresponding ABNF rules.

requirements.section: Conformance > Requirements Notation
requirements.text: Within a given message, a sender MUST NOT generate protocol elements or syntax alternatives that are only allowed to be generated by participants in other roles (i.e., a role that the sender does not have for that message).

requirements.section: Conformance > Length Requirements
requirements.text: At a minimum, a recipient MUST be able to parse and process protocol element lengths that are at least as long as the values that it generates for those same protocol elements in other messages.

requirements.section: Conformance > Length Requirements
requirements.text: A recipient SHOULD parse a received protocol element defensively, with only marginal expectations that the element will conform to its ABNF grammar and fit within a reasonable buffer size.

requirements.section: Conformance > Error Handling
requirements.text: Unless noted otherwise, a recipient MAY attempt to recover a usable protocol element from an invalid construct.

requirements.section: Conformance > Error Handling
requirements.text: A recipient MUST interpret a received protocol element according to the semantics defined for it by this specification, including extensions to this specification, unless the recipient has determined (through experience or configuration) that the sender incorrectly implements what is implied by those semantics.

requirements.section: Terminology and Core Concepts > Connections, Clients, and Servers
requirements.text: As a result, a server MUST NOT assume that two requests on the same connection are from the same user agent unless the connection is secured and specific to that agent.

requirements.section: Terminology and Core Concepts > Caches
requirements.text: Any client or server MAY employ a cache, though a cache cannot be used while acting as a tunnel.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > URI References
requirements.text: It is RECOMMENDED that all senders and recipients support, at a minimum, URIs with lengths of 8000 octets in protocol elements.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > http URI Scheme
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate an "http" URI with an empty host identifier.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > http URI Scheme
requirements.text: A recipient that processes such a URI reference MUST reject it as invalid.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > https URI Scheme
requirements.text: A client MUST ensure that its HTTP requests for an "https" resource are secured, prior to being communicated, and that it only accepts secured responses to those requests.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > https URI Scheme
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate an "https" URI with an empty host identifier.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > https URI Scheme
requirements.text: A recipient that processes such a URI reference MUST reject it as invalid.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > http(s) Normalization and Comparison
requirements.text: Two HTTP URIs that are equivalent after normalization (using any method) can be assumed to identify the same resource, and any HTTP component MAY perform normalization.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > http(s) Normalization and Comparison
requirements.text: As a result, distinct resources SHOULD NOT be identified by HTTP URIs that are equivalent after normalization (using any method defined in Section 6.2 of [URI]).

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > Deprecation of userinfo in http(s) URIs
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate the userinfo subcomponent (and its "@" delimiter) when an "http" or "https" URI reference is generated within a message as a target URI or field value.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > HTTP-Related URI Schemes > Deprecation of userinfo in http(s) URIs
requirements.text: Before making use of an "http" or "https" URI reference received from an untrusted source, a recipient SHOULD parse for userinfo and treat its presence as an error; it is likely being used to obscure the authority for the sake of phishing attacks.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > http Origins
requirements.text: When an "http" URI is used within a context that calls for access to the indicated resource, a client MAY attempt access by resolving the host identifier to an IP address, establishing a TCP connection to that address on the indicated port, and sending over that connection an HTTP request message containing a request target that matches the client's target URI (Section 7.1).

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Origins
requirements.text: When an "https" URI is used within a context that calls for access to the indicated resource, a client MAY attempt access by resolving the host identifier to an IP address, establishing a TCP connection to that address on the indicated port, securing the connection end-to-end by successfully initiating TLS over TCP with confidentiality and integrity protection, and sending over that connection an HTTP request message containing a request target that matches the client's target URI (Section 7.1).

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: Automated clients MUST log the error to an appropriate audit log (if available) and SHOULD terminate the connection (with a bad certificate error).

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: Automated clients MAY provide a configuration setting that disables this check, but MUST provide a setting which enables it.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: If the certificate is not valid for the target URI's origin, a user agent MUST either obtain confirmation from the user before proceeding (see Section 3.5) or terminate the connection with a bad certificate error.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: The client MUST construct a reference identity from the service's host: if the host is a literal IP address (Section 4.3.5), the reference identity is an IP-ID, otherwise the host is a name and the reference identity is a DNS-ID.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: To establish a secured connection to dereference a URI, a client MUST verify that the service's identity is an acceptable match for the URI's origin server.

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: In general, a client MUST verify the service identity using the verification process defined in Section 6 of [RFC6125].

requirements.section: Identifiers in HTTP > Authoritative Access > https Certificate Verification
requirements.text: A reference identity of type CN-ID MUST NOT be used by clients.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Names
requirements.text: A proxy MUST forward unrecognized header fields unless the field name is listed in the Connection header field (Section 7.6.1) or the proxy is specifically configured to block, or otherwise transform, such fields.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Names
requirements.text: Other recipients SHOULD ignore unrecognized header and trailer fields.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Order
requirements.text: A recipient MAY combine multiple field lines within a field section that have the same field name into one field line, without changing the semantics of the message, by appending each subsequent field line value to the initial field line value in order, separated by a comma (",") and optional whitespace (OWS, defined in Section 5.6.3).

requirements.section: Fields > Field Order
requirements.text: This means that, aside from the well-known exception noted below, a sender MUST NOT generate multiple field lines with the same name in a message (whether in the headers or trailers) or append a field line when a field line of the same name already exists in the message, unless that field's definition allows multiple field line values to be recombined as a comma-separated list (i.e., at least one alternative of the field's definition allows a comma-separated list, such as an ABNF rule of #(values) defined in Section 5.6.1).

requirements.section: Fields > Field Order
requirements.text: The order in which field lines with the same name are received is therefore significant to the interpretation of the field value; a proxy MUST NOT change the order of these field line values when forwarding a message.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Order
requirements.text: A server MUST NOT apply a request to the target resource until it receives the entire request header section, since later header field lines might include conditionals, authentication credentials, or deliberately misleading duplicate header fields that could impact request processing.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Limits
requirements.text: A client MAY discard or truncate received field lines that are larger than the client wishes to process if the field semantics are such that the dropped value(s) can be safely ignored without changing the message framing or response semantics.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Limits
requirements.text: A server that receives a request header field line, field value, or set of fields larger than it wishes to process MUST respond with an appropriate 4xx (Client Error) status code.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Values
requirements.text: Field values containing other CTL characters are also invalid; however, recipients MAY retain such characters for the sake of robustness when they appear within a safe context (e.g., an application-specific quoted string that will not be processed by any downstream HTTP parser).

requirements.section: Fields > Field Values
requirements.text: Field values containing CR, LF, or NUL characters are invalid and dangerous, due to the varying ways that implementations might parse and interpret those characters; a recipient of CR, LF, or NUL within a field value MUST either reject the message or replace each of those characters with SP before further processing or forwarding of that message.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Values
requirements.text: When a specific version of HTTP allows such whitespace to appear in a message, a field parsing implementation MUST exclude such whitespace prior to evaluating the field value.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Values
requirements.text: A recipient SHOULD treat other allowed octets in field content (i.e., obs-text) as opaque data.

requirements.section: Fields > Field Values
requirements.text: Specifications for newly defined fields SHOULD limit their values to visible US-ASCII octets (VCHAR), SP, and HTAB.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Lists (#rule ABNF Extension) > Sender Requirements
requirements.text: In any production that uses the list construct, a sender MUST NOT generate empty list elements.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Lists (#rule ABNF Extension) > Recipient Requirements
requirements.text: In other words, a recipient MUST accept lists that satisfy the following syntax:

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Lists (#rule ABNF Extension) > Recipient Requirements
requirements.text: A recipient MUST parse and ignore a reasonable number of empty list elements: enough to handle common mistakes by senders that merge values, but not so much that they could be used as a denial-of-service mechanism.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Whitespace
requirements.text: Any content known to be defined as BWS MAY be removed before interpreting it or forwarding the message downstream.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Whitespace
requirements.text: Any content known to be defined as OWS or RWS MAY be replaced with a single SP before interpreting it or forwarding the message downstream.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Whitespace
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate BWS in messages.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Whitespace
requirements.text: A recipient MUST parse for such bad whitespace and remove it before interpreting the protocol element.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Whitespace
requirements.text: For protocol elements where optional whitespace is preferred to improve readability, a sender SHOULD generate the optional whitespace as a single SP; otherwise, a sender SHOULD NOT generate optional whitespace except as needed to overwrite invalid or unwanted protocol elements during in-place message filtering.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Whitespace
requirements.text: A sender SHOULD generate RWS as a single SP.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Quoted Strings
requirements.text: Recipients that process the value of a quoted-string MUST handle a quoted-pair as if it were replaced by the octet following the backslash.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Quoted Strings
requirements.text: A sender SHOULD NOT generate a quoted-pair in a comment except where necessary to quote parentheses ["(" and ")"] and backslash octets occurring within that comment.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Quoted Strings
requirements.text: A sender SHOULD NOT generate a quoted-pair in a quoted-string except where necessary to quote DQUOTE and backslash octets occurring within that string.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Date/Time Formats
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate additional whitespace in an HTTP-date beyond that specifically included as SP in the grammar.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Date/Time Formats
requirements.text: A recipient that parses a timestamp value in an HTTP field MUST accept all three HTTP-date formats.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Date/Time Formats
requirements.text: Recipients of a timestamp value in rfc850-date format, which uses a two-digit year, MUST interpret a timestamp that appears to be more than 50 years in the future as representing the most recent year in the past that had the same last two digits.

requirements.section: Fields > Common Rules for Defining Field Values > Date/Time Formats
requirements.text: When a sender generates a field that contains one or more timestamps defined as HTTP-date, the sender MUST generate those timestamps in the IMF-fixdate format.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Control Data
requirements.text: A client MAY send a lower request version if it is known that the server incorrectly implements the HTTP specification, but only after the client has attempted at least one normal request and determined from the response status code or header fields (e.g., Server) that the server improperly handles higher request versions.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Control Data
requirements.text: A client MUST NOT send a version to which it is not conformant.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Control Data
requirements.text: A server MUST NOT send a version to which it is not conformant.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Control Data
requirements.text: A client SHOULD send a request version equal to the highest version to which the client is conformant and whose major version is no higher than the highest version supported by the server, if this is known.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Control Data
requirements.text: A recipient that receives a message with a major version number that it implements and a minor version number higher than what it implements SHOULD process the message as if it were in the highest minor version within that major version to which the recipient is conformant.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Control Data
requirements.text: A server SHOULD send a response version equal to the highest version to which the server is conformant that has a major version less than or equal to the one received in the request.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Trailer Fields > Limitations on Use of Trailers
requirements.text: A recipient MUST NOT merge a trailer field into a header section unless the recipient understands the corresponding header field definition and that definition explicitly permits and defines how trailer field values can be safely merged.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Trailer Fields > Limitations on Use of Trailers
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT generate a trailer field unless the sender knows the corresponding header field name's definition permits the field to be sent in trailers.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Trailer Fields > Limitations on Use of Trailers
requirements.text: Because of the potential for trailer fields to be discarded in transit, a server SHOULD NOT generate trailer fields that it believes are necessary for the user agent to receive.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Trailer Fields > Processing Trailer Fields
requirements.text: At the end of a message, a recipient MAY treat the set of received trailer fields as a data structure of name/value pairs, similar to (but separate from) the header fields.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Trailer Fields > Processing Trailer Fields
requirements.text: Trailer fields that might be generated more than once during a message MUST be defined as a list-based field even if each member value is only processed once per field line received.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Date
requirements.text: A recipient with a clock that receives a response with an invalid Date header field value MAY replace that value with the time that response was received.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Date
requirements.text: A user agent MAY send a Date header field in a request, though generally will not do so unless it is believed to convey useful information to the server.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Date
requirements.text: An origin server without a clock MUST NOT generate a Date header field.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Date
requirements.text: An origin server with a clock (as defined in Section 5.6.7) MUST generate a Date header field in all 2xx (Successful), 3xx (Redirection), and 4xx (Client Error) responses, and MAY generate a Date header field in 1xx (Informational) and 5xx (Server Error) responses.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Date
requirements.text: A recipient with a clock that receives a response message without a Date header field MUST record the time it was received and append a corresponding Date header field to the message's header section if it is cached or forwarded downstream.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Date
requirements.text: A sender that generates a Date header field SHOULD generate its field value as the best available approximation of the date and time of message generation.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction > Message Metadata > Trailer
requirements.text: A sender that intends to generate one or more trailer fields in a message SHOULD generate a Trailer header field in the header section of that message to indicate which fields might be present in the trailers.

requirements.section: Message Abstraction
requirements.text: However, a client MUST retain knowledge of the request when parsing, interpreting, or caching a corresponding response.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Determining the Target Resource
requirements.text: These forms MUST NOT be used with other methods.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Host and :authority
requirements.text: A user agent MUST generate a Host header field in a request unless it sends that information as an ":authority" pseudo-header field.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Host and :authority
requirements.text: A user agent that sends Host SHOULD send it as the first field in the header section of a request.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Rejecting Misdirected Requests
requirements.text: In particular, a request for an "https" resource MUST be rejected unless it has been received over a connection that has been secured via a certificate valid for that target URI's origin, as defined by Section 4.2.2.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Rejecting Misdirected Requests
requirements.text: Unless the connection is from a trusted gateway, an origin server MUST reject a request if any scheme-specific requirements for the target URI are not met.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Response Correlation
requirements.text: A client that receives a response while it is still sending the associated request SHOULD continue sending that request unless it receives an explicit indication to the contrary (see, e.g., Section 9.5 of [HTTP/1.1] and Section 6.4 of [HTTP/2]).

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Message Forwarding > Connection
requirements.text: When a field aside from Connection is used to supply control information for or about the current connection, the sender MUST list the corresponding field name within the Connection header field.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Message Forwarding > Connection
requirements.text: Intermediaries MUST parse a received Connection header field before a message is forwarded and, for each connection-option in this field, remove any header or trailer field(s) from the message with the same name as the connection-option, and then remove the Connection header field itself (or replace it with the intermediary's own control options for the forwarded message).

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Message Forwarding > Connection
requirements.text: A sender MUST NOT send a connection option corresponding to a field that is intended for all recipients of the content.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Message Forwarding > Connection
requirements.text: Furthermore, intermediaries SHOULD remove or replace fields that are known to require removal before forwarding, whether or not they appear as a connection-option, after applying those fields' semantics.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Message Forwarding > Max-Forwards
requirements.text: A recipient MAY ignore a Max-Forwards header field received with any other request methods.

requirements.section: Routing HTTP Messages > Message Forwarding > Max-Forwards
requirements.text: Each intermediary that receives a TRACE or OPTIONS request containing a Max-Forwards header field MUST check and update its value prior to forwarding the request.
